Shiny" subtitle: Day 22 title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: ../img/shiny-logo.png data-background-size: 40% data-background-position: right data-background-opacity: "0.8" data-slide-number: none format: revealjs: incremental: true code-copy: true code-link: true scrollable: true auto-stretch: false editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- # Shiny: High level view ## Every Shiny app has a webpage that the user visits,
and behind this webpage there is a computer that serves this webpage by running R. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../img/shiny-high-level-1.png){width=80%} ::: ::: ## {.center} When running your app locally, the computer serving your app is your computer. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../img/shiny-high-level-2.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## {.center} When your app is deployed, the computer serving your app is a web server. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../img/shiny-high-level-3.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## {.center} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../img/shiny-high-level-4.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## Demo ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## Getting started ::: {.nonincremental} Option 1: Embed a shiny plot/table in HTML docs - Need add `runtime: shiny` to your YAML header ::: . . . ::: {.nonincremental} Option 2: Can create an `app.R` file with a `ui()` and `server()` function - For template
`New Files > R Markdown > Shiny - New Files > Shiny Web App` ::: ## What's in an app? ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( inputs, outputs ) server <- function( ) { ... } ` shinyApp( ui = ui, server = server ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} - **User interface** controls the layout and appearance of app - **Server function** contains instructions needed to build app ::: ::: ## Data: Ask a manager Source: Ask a Manager Survey via [TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/master/data/2021/2021-05-18) > This data does not reflect the general population; it reflects Ask a Manager readers who self-selected to respond, which is a very different group (as you can see just from the demographic breakdown below, which is very white and very female). Some findings [here](https://www.askamanager.org/2021/05/some-findings-from-24000-peoples-salaries.html). ## Data: `manager` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} manager <- read_csv(here(here(), "data/manager-survey.csv")) manager ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 26,232 × 18 timestamp how_old_are_you industry job_title additional_context_o…¹ 1 4/27/2021 11:02:10 25-34 Educatio… Research… 2 4/27/2021 11:02:22 25-34 Computin… Change &… 3 4/27/2021 11:02:38 25-34 Accounti… Marketin… 4 4/27/2021 11:02:41 25-34 Nonprofi… Program … 5 4/27/2021 11:02:42 25-34 Accounti… Accounti… 6 4/27/2021 11:02:46 25-34 Educatio… Scholarl… 7 4/27/2021 11:02:51 25-34 Publishi… Publishi… 8 4/27/2021 11:03:00 25-34 Educatio… Librarian High school, FT 9 4/27/2021 11:03:01 45-54 Computin… Systems … Data developer/ETL De… 10 4/27/2021 11:03:02 35-44 Accounti… Senior A… # ℹ 26,222 more rows # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​additional_context_on_job_title # ℹ 13 more variables: annual_salary , other_monetary_comp , # currency , currency_other , additional_context_on_income , # country , state , city , # overall_years_of_professional_experience , # years_of_experience_in_field , … ``` ::: ::: ## Shiny vs. plotly - **Shiny** graphs need to be "connected" to RStudio or an Rstudio server + Why? Data sets are rewrangled and a new graphic is drawn - **plotly** isn't changing the underlying data set/stats being displayed, can be displayed on webpage without an RStudio session ## Ultimate goal ::: {.medium .center-align} [https://minecr.shinyapps.io/manager-survey](https://minecr.shinyapps.io/manager-survey/) ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ## Your turn 1. Add `filter` code to `manager_survey_filtered` in the server function 2. Add output code for filtered data in ui function Check that it works 1. Edit `output$selected_industries` so that it prints the right message 2. 1. add selected industries to checkbox list at startup 2. ## Your turn 1. Move the data processing code to a separate R script, and write the final dataset to "manager-survey-processed.rds" using `write_rds` 1. Edit the plotting code in the server function 2. Add labels to the tabPanels in the ui function and map them to the right outputID ## Your turn ## Final details - Shiny apps need to be "connected" to RStudio or a remote RStudio server - You can deploy shiny apps online + using Posit's cloud server (free/fee) - https://www.shinyapps.io/ + creating a shiny server

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
